His results vs. our past forecasts

build.note: Ice time × production per 60 minutes, both recency-weighted and blended with a position average, then scaled by how many goals the opponent allows compared with the league. Then adjusted for how he has done against our own forecasts: 187 points against 185 forecast in his earlier games, shrunk toward no adjustment. The model then turns this average into the chance of each count.

blend.detail: Recency-weighted games; the rest is the position average

blend.detail: Recency-weighted games; the rest is the position average

trend.label: assists
trend.note: Faded games count less. A game’s weight halves every 110 of his games for production and every 14 of his games for ice time.

missing: The starting goalie (team defense blends its goalies)

versus.note: History only, not a model input. In our backtests, results against one opponent did not predict the next meeting beyond a player’s overall form.

player_context.note: Newer appearances carry more weight. Ice time has a 14-appearance half-life; production per minute has a 110-appearance half-life. The offseason does not age player history. Expected shots scale with the opponent’s shots allowed, and scoring with its goals allowed, relative to the league. A player who has consistently beaten (or missed) our earlier forecasts gets a shrunk adjustment toward that record. Observed averages below are unweighted. Participation and current role remain unconfirmed.

key_drivers: Projected ice time 19.6 minutes; separately shrunk production rate
uncertainties: Line and power-play assignment not verified
invalidation_conditions: New goalie, lineup or injury information
rows.goalie_assumption: Projected, not confirmed. Opposing goalie, Utah Mammoth: likely Karel Vejmelka 77% (sv 0.896), Sebastian Cossa 23%.
rows.lineup_assumption: Participation required for action; current role and active lineup unconfirmed

sensitivity.assumption: Production/opportunity means ±10%; not a confidence interval

assessment.reason: The model and market roughly agree. The offered +265 is longer than the market-implied price, and the edge survives the sensitivity range. Toronto's depleted forward group is a meaningful risk.
assessment.model_case: A projected mean near 0.39 assists means the case relies on hitting at least one. The projection of 19.6 minutes is plausible for a top defenseman, and no single adjustment appears to be doing outsized work. The modest model-market gap is reassuring rather than suspicious.
assessment.price_case: The main line is 0.5 at +265, with break-even a little above one-in-four. Both the model and the single other book imply a shorter fair price, around +210 to +220. Most of the value is price shopping, and one comparison book is thin coverage.
assessment.context_case: Toronto is listed without several forwards. That could reduce finishers on Rielly's passes, or increase his power-play involvement. The net effect is uncertain, and it is unknown whether the model reflects these absences.

qualitative_review.countercase: With multiple Toronto forwards listed out, fewer skilled finishers may convert Rielly's setups, lowering his assist rate below his historical base. The edge depends on a price outlier against only one other book, which may reflect stale pricing rather than value.
open_checks: Confirm Rielly's power-play unit and partner given the forward absences

Reconfirm that +265 remains available and check other books for movement

evidence.interpretation: If Tavares is unavailable, Toronto may have less finishing talent on Rielly's units, which could depress assist chances. Altered power-play usage could partly offset that.

assessment.model_case: A projected mean near 0.39 assists means the case relies on hitting at least one. The projection of 19.6 minutes is plausible for a top defenseman, and no single adjustment appears to be doing outsized work. The modest model-market gap is reassuring rather than suspicious.
assessment.price_case: The main line is 0.5 at +265, with break-even a little above one-in-four. Both the model and the single other book imply a shorter fair price, around +210 to +220. Most of the value is price shopping, and one comparison book is thin coverage.
assessment.context_case: Toronto is listed without several forwards. That could reduce finishers on Rielly's passes, or increase his power-play involvement. The net effect is uncertain, and it is unknown whether the model reflects these absences.

qualitative_review.countercase: With multiple Toronto forwards listed out, fewer skilled finishers may convert Rielly's setups, lowering his assist rate below his historical base. The edge depends on a price outlier against only one other book, which may reflect stale pricing rather than value.

steps.label: Opponent shots allowed vs. long-run league average

build.note: Ice time × production per 60 minutes, both recency-weighted and blended with a position average, then scaled by how many shots the opponent allows compared with the league. Then adjusted for how he has done against our own forecasts: 98 shots against 102.5 forecast in his earlier games, shrunk toward no adjustment. The model then turns this average into the chance of each count.

blend.detail: Recency-weighted games; the rest is the position average

blend.detail: Recency-weighted games; the rest is the position average

trend.label: SOG
trend.note: Faded games count less. A game’s weight halves every 110 of his games for production and every 14 of his games for ice time.

missing: The starting goalie (team defense blends its goalies)

versus.note: History only, not a model input. In our backtests, results against one opponent did not predict the next meeting beyond a player’s overall form.

player_context.note: Newer appearances carry more weight. Ice time has a 14-appearance half-life; production per minute has a 110-appearance half-life. The offseason does not age player history. Expected shots scale with the opponent’s shots allowed, and scoring with its goals allowed, relative to the league. A player who has consistently beaten (or missed) our earlier forecasts gets a shrunk adjustment toward that record. Observed averages below are unweighted. Participation and current role remain unconfirmed.

key_drivers: Projected ice time 18.0 minutes; separately shrunk production rate
uncertainties: Line and power-play assignment not verified
invalidation_conditions: New goalie, lineup or injury information
rows.goalie_assumption: Projected, not confirmed. Opposing goalie, Detroit Red Wings: likely John Gibson 88% (sv 0.899), Daniil Tarasov 12%, back-to-back.
rows.lineup_assumption: Participation required for action; current role and active lineup unconfirmed

sensitivity.assumption: Production/opportunity means ±10%; not a confidence interval

rows.consensus_ev_basis: Market conditional probability with independent-model push estimate

assessment.reason: The projection sits clearly below the line and the edge holds across the sensitivity range. No sourced fact identifies a material blocker, though the size of the model-market gap calls for caution.
assessment.model_case: A projected mean near 1.1 shots, with a median of 1, against a 1.5 line favors the under. The case rests on a projection of 18 minutes and a shrunk shot rate. Power-play and pair assignment are unverified, and a power-play role would raise his shot volume.
assessment.price_case: The main line is 1.5 at -110, with break-even just above even money. The model's fair price is about -228, versus a consensus near -113 across four books. That gap is large. A weight-of-a-tenth blend lands only slightly above break-even, so the edge depends heavily on trusting the model.
assessment.context_case: Detroit's listed absences could tilt possession toward Tampa Bay, which would work against the under. Whether the model reflects this is unknown. D'Astous's own role and status are unverified.

qualitative_review.countercase: Four books cluster near even money, which suggests the market sees a meaningfully higher shot rate. A depleted Detroit lineup on a back-to-back could hand Tampa extended offensive-zone time and generate more point shots. If D'Astous plays on the power play or above 18 minutes, two shots becomes much more reachable.
